sources.title: ADXL354/ADXL355 Data Sheet
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rev D; revision history June 2025 (Rev C to Rev D)
sources.locator: pp. 4-6 (ranges/defaults); pp. 23-27 (filter and group delay); pp. 32-33 (external synchronization and sample timing)
sources.observed_operation: Manufacturer datasheet verified selectable ADXL355 ranges, power-up HPF/LPF/ODR defaults, digital filter group delay at 4 kHz, 400 kHz I2C rate limit, and external synchronization timing semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Power-up values are defaults and configurable. At 400 kHz I2C the datasheet recommends no more than 800 Hz ODR; exceeding the interface limit may cause missing samples or added noise. Synchronization modes have different delay and sample-time semantics.
sources.applicability: Supports the named ADXL355 example and acquisition audit only; it does not identify or specify the cart logger.
sources.critic_verification: Primary manufacturer source checked; investigator's bounded claims are supported.

sources.title: Measuring Vibration with Accelerometers
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current HTML; no dated release or commit displayed
sources.locator: Choosing the Right Accelerometer; Number of Axes; Weight; Mounting Options; Signal Conditioning
sources.observed_operation: Vendor guide describes accelerometer range/calibration, triaxial sensing, structure mass loading, mounting compliance, and IEPE/conditioning alternatives.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Mount-frequency examples are for a typical 100 mV/g accelerometer and are not universal. Looser attachment reduces usable frequency; added mounting mass can lower resonance.
sources.applicability: General measurement-design guidance for comparing mounts and choosing a reference; specific sensor/structure limits must be checked.
sources.critic_verification: Primary vendor source checked; the draft scopes numeric mounting examples.

sources.title: EVAL-ADXL355Z Linux command line for setting the sample frequency
sources.released_version_or_commit: Q&A opened 2023-04-12; verified vendor response 2023-05-15; EVAL-ADXL355Z, PetaLinux 2022.2/Linux 5.15.36, IIO over SPI at 6.25 MHz
sources.locator: Setup lines 278-297; support response and interrupt counts lines 346-365
sources.observed_operation: User reported 4 kHz configured but approximately 2 kHz effective. Vendor support described missed data-ready interrupts reproduced on a Raspberry Pi path and suggested servicing the hardware FIFO on FIFO-full.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Specific non-real-time Linux interrupt path. The FIFO approach was proposed for future work; the thread does not confirm a shipped fix.
sources.applicability: A bounded implementation failure mode motivating effective-rate/loss checks; not evidence of a general ADXL355 defect or cart behavior.
sources.critic_verification: Original user and vendor posts checked; automated page summary was not used as sole evidence.

sources.title: Simultaneous Measurements of the Vehicle, Track, and Soil Vibrations at a Surface, Bridge, and Tunnel Railway Line
sources.released_version_or_commit: 2017 version of record; DOI 10.1155/2017/1959286; underlying field campaign in 1994
sources.locator: Sections 2.1-2.4 and 4-5; especially measurement equipment and speed comparisons
sources.observed_operation: Primary field report describes simultaneous vehicle, track, and soil measurements on a 3 km German high-speed line, vehicle piezoelectric accelerometers, track/soil geophones, multiple track positions, and speed-varying train passages. The 72-channel 2 kHz setup is specified for the surface section; smaller systems served other sections and the vehicle.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Passenger train, measuring car axle load 100 kN and wheelset mass 1500 kg, specified railway structures and speeds. Sampling-rate details vary by section.
sources.applicability: Supports multi-location synchronized reference and speed-comparison methods; no cart thresholds, amplitudes, diagnosis, or safety transfer.

sources.title: Assessment of integration method for displacement determination using field accelerometer and geophone data
sources.released_version_or_commit: 2017 version of record; Journal of Zhejiang University Science A 18(7), 553-566; DOI 10.1631/jzus.A1600212
sources.locator: Abstract; field-study methods/results and conclusions, pp. 553-566
sources.observed_operation: Primary field study compares accelerometer/geophone-derived displacement with sleeper LVDT in a conventional French railway track. It discusses filtering, loading wavelength, repeatability, speed and axle-load validity; analyzed results include 1790 intercity passages and a stated 80-200 km/h, 105-225 kN/axle validity range.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Specific rail track-bed displacement method, sensor placements, speeds, axle loads, and filtering assumptions; the study's validity range is not transferable.
sources.applicability: Supports use of independent reference instruments and explicit load/speed/filter validity; it does not validate cart vibration or fault diagnosis.
sources.critic_verification: Official journal full text checked through the journal's official text/PDF endpoint.

sources.title: Experimental Study of Wheel-to-Rail Interaction Using Acceleration Sensors for Continuous Rail Transport Comfort Evaluation
sources.released_version_or_commit: 2023-09-25 version of record; Sensors 23(19):8064, DOI 10.3390/s23198064; page notes updates through 2026-08-27
sources.locator: Sections 2.1-2.4 and 4; tables 4-5; sensor placement and acquisition description
sources.observed_operation: Primary rail-wagon study uses multiple axle-box and car-body sensor positions, compares loaded and unloaded conditions, and reports 50 ms (20 Hz) collection intervals with six active channels.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Specific wagon/test-center comfort evaluation and its sensor/acquisition design. The reported rate does not establish high-frequency defect-impact capture.
sources.applicability: Method precedent for load and sensor-position comparisons only; no cart threshold or diagnostic transfer.

sources.title: Order tracking — Dewesoft X Manual EN
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current online Dewesoft X manual page; no release date or pinned version displayed
sources.locator: Overview/hardware notes; setup sample rate; frequency-channel settings for counters, RPM, and signal tracking
sources.observed_operation: Vendor module manual calls for an accelerometer plus angle/RPM input, describes a 10 kHz rate as needed in many cases, and distinguishes angle-sensor phase from RPM/signal-tracked estimates.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Dewesoft product/module guidance, not a universal sample-rate requirement. RPM/signal tracking lacks zero-angle/key-phasor phase.
sources.applicability: Optional wheel-order-analysis reference only; does not locate events along the cart route or diagnose a fault.

sources.title: A methodology for the measurement of track geometry based on computer vision and inertial sensors
sources.observed_operation: Primary methods preprint describes a rail-mounted system using cameras, an IMU, and a position signal that may come from odometer, GNSS, or wheel encoder; it requires a rigid installation, visible rail heads, and camera calibration.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Proposed track-geometry system for railway vehicles, not a demonstrated cart implementation. The unversioned arXiv landing URL is mutable; the reviewed v1 URL is recorded separately.
sources.applicability: Spatial-reference precedent only; it does not establish cart location accuracy, fault detection, or safety.
sources.critic_verification: Version-pinned v1 abstract and HTML checked; same source ID retained and the locator caveat is explicit.
